target_customer: Engineer-to-order manufacturers and defense and engineering organizations that quote, design and support custom products
problem: Engineer-to-order companies keep designs, test data, ERP records and documents in scattered systems, making quoting, compliance and onboarding slow. Capuchin makes them searchable and automates work on the customer's own infrastructure.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software deployed on customer infrastructure; pricing not found
product_category: On-premise AI search and automation for engineering organizations

founders.name: Jackson Roberts
education: University of Colorado Boulder, class of 2021
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as software engineer and the only founder, with a team size of 5.

competitors.name: Tacton
competitors.what: Engineer-to-order CPQ and design automation inside SolidWorks, Creo and Inventor
competitors.traction_then: Established vendor named by analysts as an ETO CPQ leader

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing CAD, PDM and ERP data into search is standard engineering with hard integration work; on-premise deployment with language models became harder to build and later more important.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations with PDM and ERP systems and on-premise deployment help, but enterprise search and CPQ vendors could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying Capuchin.

market_need_then: Engineer-to-order firms spend heavily on configuration and quoting software (Tacton and Configit serve them), but no Capuchin-specific demand evidence was found.

identity.logo: Capuchin logo shown on the site; details not described by the source
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Sovereign AI for engineering organizations

brand_strength.rationale: Search results about the name are dominated by capuchin monkey research, and no press about the company's brand was found.

pivots.from: Search and automation for engineer-to-order companies (YC page)
pivots.to: Sovereign AI for engineering organizations running on customer infrastructure (site, 2026)
pivots.why: not stated; positioning change seen by comparing sources, date unknown

outcome_analysis: Capuchin is a one founder YC Winter 2022 company that moved from search for engineer-to-order firms to on-premise sovereign AI for engineering organizations. Its site is active in 2026 with a demo call to action and offices in several states, but no priced rounds, customers or press were found, so its trajectory is unresolved.
notes: Dealroom shows a 125K USD seed with no investors and a machine-written summary; one aggregator only, unverified, so not recorded as a round. The same 125K USD seed figure appears for Codexa, so treat the aggregator figure with caution. No funding press or SEC filing was found. Tacton is dated by a 2020 analyst note; Configit appeared in the same results with no date. The engineering document search wedge had no dated startup rival in results. Education is from the YC page; prior employers are null. Funding completeness pass: 125K seed recorded from Dealroom; date and investors hidden, null. Single database, and the same figure appears for another company.
